items.title: RGNUL faculty say dispute with Vice-Chancellor remains unresolved 3 weeks on; launch 'no cooperation' campaign
items.summary: About 3 weeks into their dispute with the administration, faculty members of Rajiv Gandhi National University of Law (RGNUL), Patiala say nothing has changed. The dispute began on August 10, when RGNUL faculty gave the University a 48-hour notice . They alleged misconduct by Vice-Chancellor (VC) Prof (Dr) Jai S Singh and sought the Chancellor's intervention. Faculty had alleged irregularities in promotions, interference in the curriculum, an opaque functioning of the VC's office and questionable appointments that bypassed the Registrar and Deans. Non-teaching staff followed with their own 48-hour notice the next day, over unresolved promotions and other service grievances. On August 12, the Vice-Chancellor issued a notice directing an end to the strike and withdrew the disputed promotion at the centre of the faculty's complaint. But faculty said at the time that he had taken no real steps to resolve the underlying issues and that a pen-down strike went ahead regardless. On August 27, the faculty wrote to the VC again asking what he was doing to resolve the situation. He gave no clear answer, they said. He then called a meeting on August 31. items.title: From Okhla to Badarpur: 5 Delhi seats that lost over 40% of their 2025 electorate
items.summary: All comparisons between deleted names and votes cast in 2025 are size comparisons only, not indications of overlap between the two groups. The draft roll as part of the Special Intensive Revision exercise is out for Delhi. Of 1,45,10,299 electors, 47,56,722 are currently out – nearly one in every three persons excluded. Seven of Delhi’s 70 constituencies recorded more than 1 lakh deletions each. In descending order in terms of sheer numbers, these are Burari, Okhla, Badarpur, Vikaspuri, Matiala, Rithala, and Karawal Nagar. In terms of deletions compared to the size of the electorate, five constituencies had more than 40 percent of their 2025 electorate missing from the draft roll. These were Tughlakabad, Okhla, R.K. Puram, Jangpura and Badarpur. Of these five, three were won by the AAP and two by the BJP in the 2025 Delhi assembly election. Tughlakabad saw the highest deletion rate. Of the 2,04,867 electors registered during the 2025 election, 92,033 are missing from the draft roll – nearly one in two voters. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday quashed several first information reports (FIRs) registered by police in Delhi, Bihar, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Assam in connection with the recent agitation led by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over academic issues including paper leaks. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi , and Justice V Mohana invoked Article 142 of the Constitution to quash the criminal cases after the Central government and respective governments moved applications to seek quashing of the cases. The Court also directed that similar FIRs in other States and Union Territories – other than Delhi, Bihar, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Assam - shall not be pursued or investigated, meaning they shall be considered closed for all intents and purposes. "Keeping in view the future prospects of the young protesters who came to participate in a peaceful protest to raise their voice in support of certain demands, we deem it appropriate to invoke our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution in order to do complete justice between the parties," the Court said. items.title: Sex with minor wife can attract offence under POCSO Act; Muslim personal law no defence: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently refused to quash a case against a man accused of repeatedly raping a 17-year-old girl, holding that the alleged marital relationship between them could not protect him from prosecution. Justice Jobin Sebastian made the observation in an order dated August 19, 2026, while dismissing a plea by the accused who claimed that the minor victim was his legally wedded wife and that their marriage had been solemnised according to Muslim religious rites. The accused had been charged under Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code as well as the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. Insofar as the POCSO offences were concerned, the Court said that even if such a marriage had taken place under Muslim personal law, it would not protect the accused from criminal liability since the girl was below the age of 18. items.title: Karnataka HC grants relief to man booked for sexual harassment after urinating near railway track
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday quashed criminal proceedings filed against a man accused of sexually harassing a woman after she came across him attending nature's call near a railway track. The complainant woman had accused the accused man of exposing his private parts to her and making certain inappropriate gestures at her. The Court, however, found that it appeared to be a case where the accused man had made some gestures out of shock when he found that the woman had seen him while he was urinating. Justice M Nagaprasanna opined that this cannot amount to the offence under Section 75 (2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), which deals with the offence of sexual harassment. The Court, therefore, allowed the accused man's plea to quash the criminal case against him. " The petitioner admittedly, even according to the complaint, was answering a nature's call ... after searching for a public toilet all over and not finding it ... items.title: Collegium recommends Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Jammu & Kashmir High Court Chief Justice
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Justice Bhati is currently a judge of the Rajasthan High Court. The decision to recommend his name for Chief Justice was taken by the collegium at a meeting held on August 31. If the Centre confirms the collegium's recommendation, Justice Bhati will take over as Chief Justice from Justice Sanjeev Kumar who has been serving as acting Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh since June 2. Justice Bhati was a lawyer practicing across several areas of law for nearly 25 before he was elevated to the bench of the Rajasthan High Court on November 16, 2016. As a lawyer, he served as a Additional Advocate General for the State and was elected as President of the High Court Lawyers Association at different points Justice Bhati's wife, Justice Nupur Bhati, was also elevated as a judge of the Rajasthan High Court in 2023. items.title: Candidates can claim reservation in Puducherry based on mother's native origin even if father is a migrant: Madras HC
items.summary: The Madras High Court has held that candidates born and raised in Puducherry can claim Scheduled Caste (SC), Most Backward Class (MBC), and Other Backward Class (OBC) reservation benefits based on their mother's native origin status even if their father is a migrant from outside the Union Territory [Thelagam vs Union Territory of Puducherry] By way of an order passed on August 27, Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy allowed a batch of 28 petitions and set aside orders of the Union Territory administration that had refused or downgraded community certificates to "migrant" status solely because the petitioners' fathers, though of the same caste as their mothers, had moved to Puducherry from other States. The Court rejected Puducherry's position that caste status must be traced through the father since Indian society is patriarchal. The Court ruled that such reasoning cannot be sustained under Articles 14, 15 and 16 of the Constitution, particularly after the 2004 amendment to the Hindu Succession Act gave women equal coparcenary rights.
